title: Social outcomes satisfy independence of irrelevant alternatives
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ map profiles of pairwise votes on three candidates to a social sign outcome. The social outcome obtained by applying $f$ to each contest's pairwise votes satisfies independence of irrelevant alternatives: for any contest and any two ranking profiles, if every individual casts the same vote in that contest under both profiles, then the social outcomes in that contest agree.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a function from $n$-voter Boolean vote profiles to sign outcomes
